key_insight: A conductive GaOx hole transport layer can be formed during CuInSe2 growth and, when optimized, enables high-voltage 1.0 eV bottom cells without requiring extra Cu or Na.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a scalable back-contact/passivation strategy for tandem-ready CuInSe2 bottom cells, improving efficiency while avoiding heavy-alkali or Ag additions.
method: Formed GaOx as a hole transport layer by ion exchange during co-evaporation of the low-bandgap absorber.
Compared conductivity and device performance versus Cu addition, Na presence, and oxygen flow during oxide sputtering.
Evaluated whether the GaOx layer was crystalline and whether it reduced recombination at the back contact.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV for a 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cell.
watch_item: GaOx performance appears sensitive to how the layer forms and is structurally realized, so process control may be critical for reproducibility.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
